title: A startup raised $50M for a cap that turns thoughts into text

scenes.narration: Did you know a startup wants you to talk to AI just by thinking, in a baseball cap? It's called Sabi, and investors just bet fifty million dollars on it.
This week, Sabi announced a fifty million dollar seed round led by Khosla Ventures. The goal: a cap that turns words you imagine into text.
scenes.headline: Sabi raises $50M to build a cap that turns imagined words into text

scenes.narration: The idea behind it is called EEG. Your brain fires tiny electrical signals, and sensors outside your head can pick them up. No surgery.
scenes.definition: Reading the brain's tiny electrical signals from outside the head.

scenes.narration: The catch? Brain implants sit inside the skull and get the clearest signals. A cap is easy to wear, but signals arrive weak and blurry through bone and hair.
scenes.verdict: Easier to wear. Harder to read.

scenes.narration: So Sabi's trick is scale. Tens of thousands of tiny sensors feed an AI model trained on over one hundred thousand hours of recordings, to turn blurry signals into words.

steps.label: Tiny sensors
steps.sub: Tens of thousands in one cap

scenes.note: Company claims, not yet independently tested.

scenes.narration: Quick pause. If you'd wear a mind-reading cap, hit like. If not, share this with a friend and argue about it.
scenes.line: Like if you'd wear it. Share if you wouldn't.
scenes.sub: A new AI story every morning.

scenes.narration: Reports say Sabi is aiming for about thirty words per minute. Slower than typing, but with zero hands.
scenes.label: Target speed, by thought alone
scenes.sub: A company target, not a tested result.

scenes.narration: Lead investor Vinod Khosla put it this way: You cannot perform a billion brain surgeries to replace a billion keyboards.
scenes.text: You cannot perform a billion brain surgeries to replace a billion keyboards.

scenes.narration: Why does it matter? A new way to talk to computers could change how we use AI. But brain data is deeply private. And no independent tests back the claims yet.
points: A new way to talk to computers

scenes.narration: Three takeaways. One: fifty million dollars for a thought-reading cap. Two: it reads brain signals with no surgery. Three: wait for independent tests.
